title: Predict first, recall last
statement: A teaching video should have the viewer predict or tell things apart before it gives an answer, and end on a prompted recall rather than a summary.
detail: The control spec for a science video agent in the reading course plans makes it a hard rule, tagged as resting on learning evidence: at least one prediction or discrimination beat before the answer, and an outro that is a prompted recall, not a restatement (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-agent-v0.2.md`, rule 14). The video red-team lists both misses as pedagogy defects owned by the script stage: an answer that arrives before any learner operation, and a summary in place of a prompted recall (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/video-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`).
against: A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-29-staging/new-lesson-qa-invariants.md`).
